title: FUNDIS DNA Extraction
author: Harte Singer
materials: Next, arrange your area so that all of your supplies are within easy reach. I typically put the tubes to be samples to my left, then I have an empty PCR tube rack in front of me and another one to my right. Directly behind the tube rack in front of me, I have a microcentrifuge tube rack with 2 1.5mL tubes filled with autoclaved 2.5mm ball bearings. I also keep a pair of tweezers in one of the holes of the rack with the tines facing up. Next to that on the right, I have my 10 mL reagent reservoir, and on the left, a box of 100 µL pipette tips.

steps.title: Prepare workspace and reagents
steps.instruction: Clean the work area with a DNA‑destroying solution (or 70 % isopropyl rubbing alcohol, noting it does not destroy DNA) and avoid performing the extraction where PCR products are handled. Put on a fresh pair of snug‑fit gloves. Pour 2–3 mL of ES extraction buffer into a reagent reservoir.

steps.title: Receive and pre‑spin tissue samples
steps.instruction: Take the batch of 96 tissue samples that arrive in individually‑capped 8‑strip PCR tubes placed in a PCR tube rack, and spin the tubes down for 00:00:10 (10 seconds).

steps.title: Add ES extraction buffer
steps.instruction: Using a 5–50 µL 8‑channel pipettor equipped with 100 µL tips, add 15–30 µL of ES extraction buffer to each tube while holding the tips above the tube openings so the tips do not touch the sample. Do not exceed 30 µL per tube. If a tip is suspected of contamination, discard it and use a new tip (tips can be purchased on eBay).

steps.title: Add ball bearings to tubes
steps.instruction: Using tweezers, drop one ball bearing into each tube of the strip, taking care not to contaminate the tweezers. If two bearings accidentally enter a tube, it is acceptable; do not attempt to retrieve any bearings.

steps.title: Close tubes and relocate strip
steps.instruction: Close the lids of the strip and move the strip to the empty rack on the right in the correct position. Repeat the ball‑bearing addition (step 4) for each subsequent strip until all tubes have been processed.

steps.title: Vortex and brief centrifuge
steps.instruction: Place each strip on a vortexer set to the maximum setting and vortex for up to 00:00:10 (10 seconds) ensuring every tube is shaken well. Then spin the tubes in a microcentrifuge for 00:00:05 (5 seconds).

steps.title: Thermal incubation of extracts
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes in a thermal cycler at 95 °C for 00:15:00 (15 minutes) followed by a hold at 12 °C to bring the temperature back down. The DNA is now extracted; you may pause and store the tubes at –20 °C until further processing.

steps.title: Post‑incubation handling
steps.instruction: If you paused after the incubation, remove the tubes from the –20 °C freezer, allow them to reach room temperature, and spin them down for 00:00:05 (5 seconds) in a microcentrifuge. If you continue directly from the previous step, no spin is needed provided there is no liquid at the top of the tubes.

steps.title: Prepare dilution solution and equipment
steps.instruction: Clean the work area again with a DNA‑destroying cleaner if possible. Set up two empty PCR tube racks, a reagent reservoir, a 50–300 µL 8‑channel pipette, and p200 pipette tips. Fill the reagent reservoir with 10 mL of Dilution Solution (DS) containing 10 mM Tris, 100 µM EDTA, and 0.3 % (mass) BSA.

steps.title: Transfer Dilution Solution to extracts
steps.instruction: As during the initial extraction, move one strip of tubes to an empty PCR tube rack and carefully open the lids, avoiding splashes or contact of liquid with gloves; change gloves if they become contaminated. Using the multichannel pipette, add 75–125 µL of DS to each tube, selecting a volume that yields approximately a 1:5 extract‑to‑dilution ratio (do not exceed 125 µL to avoid overflow). Hold the pipette well above the tube openings, dispense gently to prevent splashing, and if a large amount misses the tube, add the remainder with a single‑channel pipette. Prioritize avoiding cross‑contamination; change tips if you are concerned, noting that tips are inexpensive compared with the precious samples.

steps.title: Store diluted DNA extracts
steps.instruction: Store the diluted extractions at –20 °C for future use, or use them immediately for PCR and then keep them at –20 °C.
